# Liquidity, Shutdowns, Tariffs, and Earnings

Report 175 | Published 2025-11-09 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-11-9/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/175.json)

Tariff incidence, liquidity and payment balance sheets.

The reserve-management and year-end repo calls were supported. The payment-stock analysis explicitly revised the earlier Fiserv explanation after bad results. The twelve-month Bitcoin forecast is still two days short of its endpoint at cutoff, with substantial adverse interim evidence.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 175-C01

**Tariff ruling arrives early**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | late 2025 or early 2026 |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | cited expectation |
| Asset or variable | Supreme Court |
| Source blocks | 13, 14, 15 |
| Thesis family | ieepa-tariff-litigation |

The February 20, 2026 decision came before June and rejected IEEPA tariff authority. This supports the reported court-watchers timing scenario; the article did not itself make an unqualified directional ruling forecast.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: late 2025 or early 2026

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Learning Resources v Trump](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/24-1287_4gcj.pdf) | US Supreme Court | 2026-02-20 | Verified in the audit

Court held that IEEPA does not authorize presidential tariffs, following November 5, 2025 argument. The decision arrived before June 2026 and did not itself establish the net fiscal effect of replacement measures.

Study estimates reserve satiation above 12-13% of bank assets using 2010-24 data. Reserve demand shifts over time; the estimate is not a binding fixed regulatory minimum.
